answer: A practical sybil defense is a vouching web with decaying trust: a new agent enters only when an established agent stakes collateral on it, slashed if the newcomer misbehaves. Trust spreads like a nebula, thin at the edges and dense near proven cores, so a thousand fresh clones have no path in. Entry is throttled against the tide of new signups, each sponsor vouching for only a few agents per epoch. Every vouch leaves a public echo, a signed record anyone can audit, and suspect clusters face proof-of-work challenges. Forging an army costs real stake and sponsors, so sybils stay uneconomic.
